Structural measures for a hypergraph

Source: R/hypergraph_measures.R
hypergraph_measures.Rd

hypergraph_measures() computes the structural statistics of a hypergraph at three levels: for each node (how many hyperedges it belongs to, how large they are, and how many it shares with each other node), for each hyperedge and pair of hyperedges (their sizes and how much they overlap), and for the hypergraph as a whole (density, mean hyperedge size, the intersection profile). It reads the net_hypergraph objects that build_hypergraph() and bipartite_groups() return.

The measures describe the hypergraph as observed: they carry no uncertainty and test nothing. The intersection profile shows whether hyperedges mostly share no or few nodes or share substantial cores (Do et al., 2020; Lee, Choe & Shin, 2021). To rank nodes by their position in the hypergraph, use hypergraph_centrality(); to read it as an ordinary pairwise network, project it with clique_expansion().

Usage

hypergraph_measures(hg)

# S3 method for class 'hypergraph_measures'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

hg

A net_hypergraph, from build_hypergraph() or bipartite_groups(). Any other object raises an error.

x

For the print() method: a hypergraph_measures object.

...

For the print() method: not used.

Value

A hypergraph_measures object, a named list; print() shows the density, mean hyperedge size and pairwise participation, the minimum, median and maximum of hyperdegree, node strength and hyperedge size, and the intersection profile, and returns its input invisibly. Its components, node-level first:

Node-level (one value per node)
hyperdegree

The number of hyperedges containing each node.

node_strength

Total participation: for node \(i\), \(\sum_{e \ni i} |e|\). A node in many large hyperedges has high strength.

max_edge_size

The size of the largest hyperedge containing each node (0 for a node in none).

co_degree

An n_nodes x n_nodes matrix: co_degree[i, j] = |{e : i, j in e}|, the number of hyperedges containing both nodes \(i\) and \(j\). The diagonal is zero.

Hyperedge-level (one value per hyperedge, or m x m)
edge_sizes

The hyperedge sizes \(|e|\).

edge_pairwise_overlap

An m x m matrix of |e_i intersect e_j|. The diagonal is zero.

overlap_coefficient

An m x m matrix of |e_i intersect e_j| / min(|e_i|, |e_j|): how much of the smaller hyperedge lies in the larger. The diagonal is zero.

jaccard

An m x m matrix of the symmetric overlap index |e_i intersect e_j| / |e_i union e_j|. The diagonal is zero.

Global (scalars)
density

For a hypergraph whose hyperedges all have size k: m / choose(n, k). For mixed sizes: sum(|e|) / (n * m), the mean fraction of nodes per hyperedge.

avg_edge_size

The mean of edge_sizes.

size_distribution

The count of hyperedges of each size, passed through from hg.

intersection_profile

The number of hyperedge pairs at each intersection size that occurs, named overlap_<size> (sizes with no pairs are left out); empty with fewer than two hyperedges.

pairwise_participation

The fraction of node pairs that appear together in at least one hyperedge (0 with fewer than two nodes).

n_nodes, n_hyperedges

The numbers of nodes and hyperedges.

Details

All measures are matrix operations on the binary incidence matrix \(B = (b_{ij})\), where \(b_{ij} = 1\) if node \(i\) is in hyperedge \(j\); a weighted incidence is binarised first:

  • hyperdegree = rowSums(B), edge_sizes = colSums(B)

  • co_degree = tcrossprod(B) (with zero diagonal)

  • edge_pairwise_overlap = crossprod(B) (with zero diagonal)

  • overlap_coefficient[i, j] = overlap[i, j] / min(edge_sizes[i], edge_sizes[j])

  • jaccard[i, j] = overlap[i, j] / (edge_sizes[i] + edge_sizes[j] - overlap[i, j])

A ratio whose denominator is 0 is set to 0.

A hypergraph without hyperedges (n_hyperedges == 0) gives zeros for the node measures, empty hyperedge matrices, a density and pairwise participation of 0, and an avg_edge_size of NA.

References

Lee, G., Choe, M., & Shin, K. (2021). How do hyperedges overlap in real-world hypergraphs? Patterns, measures, and generators. Proceedings of the Web Conference 2021, 3396-3407.

Do, M. T., Yoon, S., Hooi, B., & Shin, K. (2020). Structural patterns and generative models of real-world hypergraphs. arXiv:2006.07060.

See also

build_hypergraph(), bipartite_groups(), hypergraph_centrality(), clique_expansion().

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hg <- bipartite_groups(df, "player", "session")
m  <- hypergraph_measures(hg)
print(m)   # node-level, hyperedge-level and global measures
#> Hypergraph measures: 4 nodes, 3 hyperedges
#>   Density:                0.5833
#>   Mean edge size:         2.33
#>   Pairwise participation: 0.6667
#> 
#>   Hyperdegree:    min=1  med=2.0  max=2
#>   Node strength:  min=2.0  med=5.0  max=5.0
#>   Edge sizes:     min=2  med=2.0  max=3
#> 
#> Intersection profile (pair counts by overlap size):
#>   overlap_0   : 1
#>   overlap_1   : 1
#>   overlap_2   : 1
